_comentario: First Economics, Part 4 (summer, days 196-260): the English text of each day of Aprendo economía -- the day's story ('historia') and the text of its activity ('actividad', with its 'tipo') -- and the words of weeks 40-52 ('semanas'). Everything else is the one in content/q4.json, page by page: see cargar_ingles in tools/gen_economia.py and notes/02-english.md.

semanas.definicion: What comes first, because it is the most important.
To look at two or more things to see how they are alike and how they are different, like the prices in two shops.
What we use to find out how long or how heavy something is, the same for everyone: metres, kilos, litres.
What we write down about money: what comes in, what goes out and what is left.
How much people want to buy something: if lots of people want it and there is not much of it, the price goes up.
Something we would like to have, or would like to happen.
The work that a person knows how to do: fisherman, baker, carpenter...
The money grown-ups give children for their own things, every week or at fiesta time.
Something that is worth a lot to us, even if it does not cost any money.
What you make when you sell: the money you take, minus what you have spent.
The days when shops sell things for less than before.
To think beforehand about what you are going to do, so that you do it well.
How we use money, work and the things we have in order to live.

dias.historia: Dani is packing his suitcase for the village, and he wants to take everything: toys, storybooks, his drum... The suitcase will not shut. Mum explains that he has to think about his priority: the important things first.

actividad.pregunta: Does it go in the suitcase, or can it stay at home?

dias.historia: Lucía shows Dani how to make a list. Dani reads it very quickly and puts things from the wardrobe into the suitcase. In the end, the suitcase shuts... but a red bobble is sticking out.

actividad.pregunta: In what order do you pack a suitcase?
pasos: Put in the most important things.

dias.historia: For the summer, Dani wants a bucket for the sand by the river and a ball. With the €10 in his piggy bank, he cannot afford both: he has to decide which is his priority.
Before the trip, Mum buys what they still need. A new suitcase is very expensive, so they fix the old one, and they only buy a rucksack for Dani and a bucket.

actividad.pregunta: Mum buys a rucksack and a bucket. How much does she pay?

dias.historia: Case solved: Dani read the list so quickly that he packed his woolly hat instead of his sun hat! Luckily, Lucía saw it before they left.

checklist: I know what a priority is.
I can make a list before I pack a suitcase.
I can choose what is most important.
actividad.prompt: Draw your suitcase for the summer, with the most important things.

dias.historia: Now they are in Grandma's village. In the square there is a little shop, Carmen's grocer's, and on the main road, a big supermarket. Grandma compares them: the prices, how far away they are and how friendly they are.

actividad.pregunta: A kilo of tomatoes costs €3 at the grocer's and €2 at the supermarket. Where is it cheaper? How much do you save?

dias.historia: Lucía compares Grandma's map with the field today: the well is still there, covered with a wooden lid, but of the three poplar trees there are only two left... and a stump.

frases: Comparing means looking at how two things are alike and how they are different.
The cheapest thing is always the best.
The village shop is closer to Grandma's house.
To compare prices, you have to look at the labels.
If you compare before you buy, you spend more.

dias.historia: Carmen's grocer's sells everything: ice creams, buckets for the river beach, balls... Dani has €15 that Grandma has given him.
Andrés, Grandma's neighbour, says that he shops in both places: at the village shop for everyday things, and at the supermarket for the whole week's shopping.

actividad.pregunta: What is good about each place?
pares: is close, and they know you

dias.historia: The tortoise stone is not in the field any more: it is in the mill garden, as Martín said. But the well is still in its place. The treasure could be close by!

checklist: I know what comparing means.
I can compare prices between two shops.
I know that the cheapest thing is not always the best.
actividad.prompt: Draw the shop in Grandma's village.

dias.historia: Dad counts ten steps from the well, towards the poplars... and ends up behind them, where there is nothing. Grandma laughs: a step is not a good measure, because everyone's step is different.

actividad.texto: Ten of Dad's steps are 8 metres, and ten of Lucía's steps are 4 metres. How many more metres are Dad's?

dias.historia: To be fair, things are measured with measures that are the same for everyone: metres, kilos, litres... In the village shop, Carmen weighs the fruit on her scales.

actividad.pregunta: What do you measure each thing with?

dias.historia: On Saturday there is a market in the village square. Grandma buys her fruit there, because the farmers bring it from their orchards, and it is cheaper by the kilo.

actividad.pregunta: A kilo of apples costs €3 at the grocer's and €2 at the market. Where is it cheaper? How much do you save?

dias.historia: Dani wants to share the apples from Grandma's garden with Martín and Lucía. To be fair, he shares them out one at a time, the way Mum taught him.

actividad.pregunta: Share 14 apples between Dani, Martín and Lucía. How many does each one get? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: Case solved: Dad's steps are much longer than an eight-year-old girl's, and Rosa was eight when she drew the map. That is why Dad did not find anything!

checklist: I know what a measure is.
I know what we measure things with.
I know that measures have to be the same for everyone.
actividad.prompt: Draw Dad and Lucía counting their steps from the well.

dias.historia: In the village, Lucía keeps a diary. On the last page she keeps her summer accounts: what she is given, what she spends and what she has left.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía's summer accounts: how much does she have left after each line?

dias.historia: Something visits Grandma's vegetable garden at night. The lettuces are fine, but the snails are disappearing. Lucía writes it all down in her diary.

frases: Keeping accounts means writing down what comes in and what goes out.
If you never write anything down, you always know what you have.
What is left is what you had, plus what comes in, take away what goes out.
Only banks keep accounts.

dias.historia: Before going to sleep, Lucía checks her accounts: she counts the money in her purse, to see if it is the same as what her diary says.

actividad.pregunta: How much money does Lucía have in her purse?

dias.historia: In the mud there are prints with five toes and claws, and at night there is snuffling by the woodpile. Who can it be?

actividad.pregunta: Lucía has €30. She puts €15 in the save jar and €10 in the spend jar. How much does she put in the share jar?

dias.historia: Case solved: the visitor to the vegetable garden is a hedgehog, which eats the snails. Grandma is delighted: it helps her look after the lettuces, and for free!

checklist: I know what accounts are.
I can write down what comes in and what goes out.
I can check that my accounts are right.
actividad.prompt: Draw a page of Lucía's diary, with her accounts.

dias.historia: Andrés keeps bees and sells his honey in the village. In August lots of people come, and they all want honey: there is a lot of demand. If there is not much honey and lots of people want it, the price goes up.

actividad.texto: In June, a jar of Andrés's honey costs €6; in August, it costs €8. How much has the price gone up?

dias.historia: Andrés puts on his beekeeper's suit to take out the honey. He explains that this year the bees have made less, because there has not been much rain and there are not many flowers.

actividad.pregunta: Does the price go up or down?
cosas: Everyone wants honey, and there is not much.
There are lots and lots of watermelons.
Everyone wants ice creams in August.
The shop has too many chestnuts.
There are not enough circus tickets.

dias.historia: Grandma likes buying from Andrés: the honey, the eggs and the lettuces are from the village, and she knows how he looks after them.

actividad.pregunta: Grandma buys a jar of honey and a dozen eggs. How much does she pay?

dias.historia: In Andrés's kitchen, someone has got into a jar of honey. The lid was only resting on top, and there is a line of little black dots coming from the lemon tree.

actividad.pregunta: What does each one like?

dias.historia: Case solved: it was the ants! Bigotes is not interested in honey, only in cheese. Now Andrés closes the jars tightly: honey is expensive this year.

checklist: I know what demand is.
I know that if lots of people want something and there is not much of it, the price goes up.
I know where honey comes from.
actividad.prompt: Draw Andrés in his beekeeper's suit.

dias.historia: In August, the whole family goes out to the mill garden to watch shooting stars. Dani says that every shooting star is a wish: he will wish for a bike... and a trip to the Moon.

actividad.pregunta: Is it a need or a wish?

dias.historia: Grandma shows them the Plough, which her father, the clockmaker, called “the night-time clock”. When she was a girl, she wished she could see the sea.

frases: A wish is something we would like to have.
Every wish can be bought.
Some wishes do not cost money.
For some wishes to come true, you have to save.
A wish is the same as a need.

dias.historia: Dani knows now that the bike will not fall from the sky with a shooting star. If he really wishes for it, he will have to save for it.

actividad.pregunta: Dani has €20 and he saves €10 every week. The bike costs €60. How many weeks will it take?

dias.historia: That night, everyone counts the shooting stars they see. Lucía sees seven; Dani says a hundred, but he fell asleep after the third.

actividad.pregunta: How do you watch shooting stars?
pasos: Look at the sky and take your time.

dias.historia: On the way home, Lucía thinks about her wish. It is not something you can buy: she wants the summer to last a little longer.

checklist: I know what a wish is.
I know that a wish is not the same as a need.
I can save to make a wish come true.
actividad.prompt: Draw your wish for a shooting star.

dias.historia: Hugo writes from the seaside: his grandad is a fisherman. He goes out in his boat before dawn, and sells the fish at the fish market. It is a very hard trade, says Hugo.

actividad.pregunta: What does each one do in their trade?

dias.historia: Each page of Hugo's letter tells about one day. Today he explains the journey of the fish: from the sea to the fish market, from the fish market to the fishmonger's, and from there to your plate.

actividad.pregunta: What is the right order? From the sea to the plate
pasos: He sells it at the fish market.
The fishmonger sells it in her shop.

dias.historia: There is no sea in the village, but on Tuesdays the fishmonger's van comes. Grandma buys fresh fish for supper.

actividad.pregunta: Grandma buys some fish and a loaf of bread. How much does she pay?

dias.historia: Hugo sends a riddle: “By day I sleep, and at night I guide the boats with my light.” It is the lighthouse! And at the end of the letter, a message in code: “Count your own steps.”

actividad.texto: Hugo's grandad sells 25 kilos of fish on Monday and 30 kilos on Tuesday. How many kilos does he sell on the two days altogether?

dias.historia: Lucía cracks Hugo's message, and suddenly she understands: to find the treasure, she has to count her own steps, the steps of an eight-year-old girl. She writes him a letter back.

checklist: I know what a trade is.
I know what a fisherman does.
I know how fish gets from the sea to my plate.
actividad.prompt: Draw the trade you like best.

dias.historia: The village fiesta is here. As every year, Grandma gives Lucía and Dani their fiesta pocket money, and Lucía splits hers between her three jars.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía has €20. She puts €10 in the save jar and €7 in the spend jar. How much does she put in the share jar?

dias.historia: In the square there are stalls selling churros, ice creams and balloons, and a tombola with teddy bears as prizes. Lucía looks at the prices before she spends anything.
Andrés cuts the grass in the field before the fireworks, so that it is safe. The fireworks are paid for by the council, with the money of all the villagers.

frases: Everyone pays together for the village fiesta.
Pocket money is the money grown-ups earn by working.
You can save a little of your pocket money.
Fireworks cost nothing.

dias.historia: The club enters a riddle poem in the fiesta competition. While they wait for the result, Dani cannot decide what to spend the rest of his pocket money on.

actividad.pregunta: Dani has €5: he can afford an ice cream or a balloon, but not both. Which would you choose?

dias.historia: The club's poem wins the competition! The answer to the riddle was the magnifying glass. The news is in the village newsletter, with a photo of the three of them... and Dani.

checklist: I know what pocket money is.
I can split my pocket money between three jars.
I know that everyone pays together for the village fiesta.
actividad.prompt: Draw the village square during the fiesta.

dias.historia: Lucía, who is eight like Rosa was, counts ten of her own steps from the well and stops next to the stump. There the grass grows differently, in a round patch. Could the treasure be there?

frases: A treasure does not have to cost money.
Only gold is treasure.
A family photo can be a treasure.
Treasures are bought in shops.

dias.historia: With Andrés's spade, they dig carefully and a rusty tin box appears. Inside there is a blue marble, an old photo and a letter: “For Rosa, when she is grown up.”

actividad.pregunta: Does it cost money?

dias.historia: In the photo, young Rosa is with her father, the clockmaker, who is holding a magnifying glass: the same magnifying glass with three lines that is Lucía's now!

actividad.prompt: Draw the photo of young Rosa with her father, who is holding the magnifying glass.

dias.historia: The letter says: “If you have grandchildren one day, teach them to look through Dad's magnifying glass.” Grandma smiles, her eyes shining. “I already have.”

actividad.pregunta: Why is each thing worth so much?
pares: she wrote it as a girl

dias.historia: Grandma keeps the tin box in her chest of drawers, next to the magnifying glass. “It is not worth any money,” she says, “but it is my greatest treasure.”

checklist: I know what a treasure is.
I know that what is worth most does not always cost money.
I can use a map to find something.
actividad.prompt: Draw your treasure: something that is worth a lot to you.

dias.historia: Dani and Martín set up a lemonade stall outside Grandma's door. They want to know if they make a profit: the money they take, minus what they have spent.

actividad.pregunta: The stall's accounts: how much is in the box after each line?

dias.historia: At the end of the afternoon, Martín counts the money they have taken, and Dani counts what they have spent. The profit is the extra money they have made.

actividad.texto: They have taken €26 and they have spent €8 on lemons, sugar and cups. How much have they made?

dias.historia: Dani and Martín share the profit equally, coin by coin. That way neither of them gets more than the other.

actividad.pregunta: Share 18 one-euro coins between Dani and Martín. How many does each one get? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: Afterwards, they bury a tin with a message for next summer. For their map, they count paving stones, “because paving stones don't grow”, says Martín.

actividad.pregunta: How do you set up a lemonade stall?
pasos: Write the price on a sign.
Count how much you have made.

dias.historia: Dani and Martín keep their map in Grandma's tin box. Next summer they will open their treasure... and set up their stall again.

checklist: I know what profit is.
I can work out what I make: what I take, minus what I spend.
I can share things out equally.

dias.historia: They go back to the city at the end of August, and the shops have their sales on: things cost less than before. Mum says it is a good time to buy what they need, but only that.

actividad.texto: A pair of trainers cost €30, and in the sales they cost €20. How much do you save?

dias.historia: In the car on the way back, everyone talks about their summer. Dani has made a comic of the best adventures, and Lucía reads it from the end to the beginning, to see how it all started!

actividad.pregunta: Do we need it, or is it just cheap?

dias.historia: Mum takes just the right amount of money for the sales shopping, and she counts it before going out: that way she knows how much she can spend.

actividad.pregunta: How much money is Mum taking for the shopping?

dias.historia: In the shop, the school bag Dani wants is reduced. Mum pays with a €50 note, and Dani watches carefully as she is given her change.
At home, Lucía finds a message from Martín in her school bag, written backwards: “See you next summer!” She reads it in a mirror and smiles.

checklist: I know what the sales are.
I can work out how much I save in the sales.
I can buy only what I need.
actividad.prompt: Draw something you would buy in the sales, because you need it.

dias.historia: Dani is going to start at big school. Before buying his school things, Mum and Dani plan it: they make a list and look at what they already have at home.

actividad.pregunta: Dani needs pencils and a book for school. How much does it all cost?

dias.historia: Lucía teaches Dani the club's rules for reading: slowly, with the magnifying glass if needed, and thinking about what you read.

frases: Planning means thinking beforehand about what you are going to do.
If you plan your shopping, you spend more.
A list helps you not to forget anything.
Looking at what you already have at home helps you save.
It is better to shop without looking at the list.

dias.historia: All of Dani's school things have his name written on them, in round, neat handwriting. Who can have written it?
Dani investigates his first case: the round handwriting, the last one to go to bed... and Toby did not bark. Who wrote his name on all his things?

actividad.pregunta: How do you plan your shopping?
pasos: Make a list of what you need.
Look at what you already have at home.
Think about how much you can spend.
Buy only what is on the list.

dias.historia: Case solved: it was Dad, just like Reader X! Dani has solved his first case all by himself, and the club makes him the fourth member of the Magnifying Glass Club.

checklist: I know what planning means.
I can make a list before I go shopping.
I can look at what I already have at home.
actividad.prompt: Draw your list of things for school.

dias.historia: Lucía is starting a new school year, and Dani is starting at big school, with Marta as his teacher. Lucía thinks about everything she has learnt about economics this year: money, saving, prices, work...

actividad.pregunta: What does each word mean?

dias.historia: On the first day of school, Hugo brings a surprise from the seaside, but he does not want to show it yet. Meanwhile, Lucía starts a new notebook to keep her accounts for the new school year.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía's accounts: how much does she have left after each line?

dias.historia: At last, Hugo shows it: a compass! His grandad, the fisherman, gave it to him. “So that we don't get lost on our next case,” he says.

actividad.pregunta: Is it saving or spending?
cosas: putting pocket money in the piggy bank
putting money aside for a bike

dias.historia: An envelope with no sender's address appears in the letterbox of the club's hut. Inside, there is a note: “Are you brave enough for a harder case?” Who can have sent it?

actividad.texto: Lucía had €45 in her piggy bank, and this summer she has put in €30. How much does she have now?

dias.historia: The Magnifying Glass Club meets in the hut: Lucía, Sofía, Hugo and Dani. They have a new case, a notebook for their accounts... and a whole year ahead of them.

checklist: I know what economics is.
I can save, choose, swap and share.
I can keep my accounts.
actividad.prompt: Draw what you have enjoyed learning most this year.
